scope: any possible ingestion, inhalation, skin splash, eye splash, injection, or toxic bite; a routing intent, not a self-care intent
patterns: my child swallowed some cleaning liquid
I took the wrong medicine dose
what do I do after swallowing a chemical
toddler may have eaten a laundry pod
breathed in fumes from a cleaner
my child ate a plant and seems okay
chemical splash and I do not know what it was
should I make someone vomit after poisoning
response: Do not make the person vomit and do not give food, drink, medicine, or a home antidote unless Poison Control or a health professional specifically tells you to. If it is safe, move away from fumes to fresh air. Contact Poison Control or your local poison center now with the product or container, amount, time, route of exposure, age, weight if known, and any symptoms. For an eye or skin chemical exposure, start the relevant water rinsing while making the call and do not delay.
red_flags: trouble breathing, seizure, collapse, or unresponsiveness
button battery, powerful magnet, or high-toxicity substance ingestion
exposure in a young child, pregnant person, or someone with chronic illness
unknown substance or unclear amount and time
